title: Longest Stretch Where Every Letter Repeats
statement:
`text` contains lowercase letters. Find the **longest substring** (a contiguous part of `text`) in which **every letter that appears at all appears at least `k` times**. Letters that do not occur in the substring do not matter.

Return the length of that substring, or `0` if there is none.
constraints: text contains only the letters a to z

examples.explanation: The letter c appears once, so no good substring contains it. The best parts are aabb (every letter twice) and dd; the longest has length 4.

hints.nudge: A normal window cannot be shrunk by a simple rule here, because adding a letter can make the window better or worse. What if you FIX how many different letters the window may contain?
hints.pattern: For each target u from 1 to 26, slide a window that holds exactly u different letters, and track how many of them already appear at least k times; the window is good when all u do.
hints.walkthrough: Checking every substring is O(n^2) (or worse). The difficulty is that a window can only be judged when you know how many different letters it should have. So try each possible number of different letters, target = 1 .. 26, and for a fixed target run a normal two-pointer window: extend to the right, and while the window has more than `target` different letters move the left end. Keep two counters: `unique` (letters currently in the window) and `enough` (letters in the window with count at least k). When unique == target and enough == target, every letter in the window appears at least k times, so the window is valid: record its length. Each target costs one pass, so the total is 26 passes: O(26 n). (Another solution splits the text at letters that occur fewer than k times in the whole text and solves the pieces recursively.)
